Indicates it concerns a rerouting for indication. Optionally proposal flights can be created and the corresponding RRP messages sent.

CodeTacticalReroutingConstraintType-AVOI.comment: The constrained location is to be avoided.

CodeTacticalReroutingConstraintType-DELT.comment: From this point onwards the level needs to be adapted by the delta flight level.

CodeTacticalReroutingConstraintType-LEVE.comment: From this point onwards the level needs to be adapted to the specified level.
From this point onwards the flight level and the speed need to be adapted to the specified values.
From this point onward the flight level and speed return/stay on its requested values.
From this point onward the flight level returns/stays on its requested level.

CodeTacticalReroutingConstraintType-VIA.comment: The constrained location is to be used.

CodeTacticalReroutingStatusType-NO_MATCH.comment: Message received did not match the proposal; rerouting has been invalidated

CodeTacticalReroutingStatusType-PRODUCED.comment: There is a valid rerouting going on, waiting to be realised by either an FPL or a CHG

CodeTacticalReroutingStatusType-REVOKED.comment: A booking was created for the proposal, but a manual operation that changed the regulation (typically deep rectify) has deleted the booking before the attempt to accept the proposal

CodeTacticalReroutingStatusType-TIMED_OU.comment: No FPL / CHG received on time

CodeTargetTimeStatusType-CANCELLED.comment: TTOT is no longer valid, and there is no new TTOT. (e.g. as indicated by C-DPI message)

CodeTargetTimeStatusType-NEW.comment: TTOT is set for the first time (e.g. as sent in E-DPI message, or a T-DPI when a C-DPI has been sent before for this flight)

CodeTargetTimeStatusType-UPDATED.comment: TTOT is changed (e.g. updates sent in T-DPI and A-DPI message)

CodeTargetTrajectoryChangeReportCapabili.comment: No capability for Trajectory Change Reports

CodeTaxiRouteModeType-AUTOMATIC.comment: Full automatic mode in which the system determines the route automatically also taking into account the constraints and procedures. It has all the features of the semi automatic mode plus some additional attributes for a full automatic mode.

CodeTaxiRouteModeType-MANUAL_MODE.comment: A mode in which the air traffic controller has to select the taxi route manually in the system.

CodeTaxiRouteModeType-SEMI_AUTOMATIC.comment: A mode in which the air traffic controller still has to enter the route manually but the system will give support on selection of routes.

CodeTaxiRouteStatusType-CLEARED.comment: May deviate from the planned Taxi Route.

CodeTaxiwayElementType-HOLDING_BAY.comment: A defined area where aircraft can be held, or bypassed, to facilitate efficient surface movement of aircraft.

CodeTaxiwayElementType-INTERSECTION.comment: Intersection element - with a runway or with a taxiway.

CodeTaxiwayElementType-RUNWAY_TURN_PAD.comment: A defined area on a land aerodrome adjacent to a runway for the purpose of completing a 180-degree turn on a runway.

CodeTaxiwayElementType-TAXIWAY_SHOULDER.comment: An area adjacent to the edge of a taxiway so prepared as to provide a transition between the taxiway and the adjacent surface.

CodeTaxiwaySectionType-TAXIWAY_INTERSECT.comment: A junction of two or more taxiways.

CodeTaxiwayType-BYPASS_HOLDING_BAY.comment: A defined area where aircraft can be bypassed to facilitate efficient surface movement of aircraft.

CodeTaxiwayType-HELICOPTER_AIR_TAXIWAY.comment: A defined path on the surface established for the air taxiing of helicopters.

CodeTaxiwayType-RAPID_EXIT_TAXIWAY.comment: A taxiway connected to a runway at an acute angle and designed to allow landing aeroplanes to turn off at higher speeds than are achieved on other exit taxiways thereby minimizing runway occupancy times.

CodeTelecomNetworkType-ACARS.comment: Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System. A datalink system that enables ground stations (airports, aircraft maintenance bases, etc.) and commercial aircraft to communicate without voice using a datalink system.

CodeTelecomNetworkType-AFTN.comment: A worldwide system of aeronautical fixed circuits provided, as part of the aeronautical fixed service, for the exchange of messages and/or digital data between aeronautical fixed stations having the same or compatible communications characteristics.

CodeTelecomNetworkType-AMHS.comment: Aeronautical Message Handling System. A standard for aeronautical ground-ground communications (e.g. for the transmission of NOTAM, Flight Plans or Meteorological Data) based on X.400 profiles. It has been defined by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO)

CodeTelecomNetworkType-INTERNET.comment: The Internet is a worldwide, publicly accessible series of interconnected computer networks that transmit data by packet switching using the standard Internet Protocol (IP)

CodeTerrainAwarenessAndGroundProximityAl.comment: TCAS with an alert envelope maximum altitude of 1250 ft.
TCAS with an alert envelope maximum altitude of 1650 ft.
TCAS with an alert envelope maximum altitude of 950 ft.

CodeTimeEventType-SUNRISE.comment: The time in the morning when the sun appears or full daylight arrives.

CodeTimeEventType-SUNSET.comment: The time in the evening when the sun disappears or daylight fades.

CodeTrajectoryElementType-AIRBORNE_SEGME.comment: The airborne segment of the trajectory describes the anticipated 4D path of the aircraft using data elements and resolution necessary to deliver a level of fidelity commensurate with requirements for each portion of the trajectory.
A portion of the airborne segment.

CodeTrajectoryElementType-ARRIVAL_SURFAC.comment: This segment describes the elements of the trajectory from the arrival runway, if applicable, to the arrival gate/stand. This segment reuses the same information items as for the departure surface segment, but in reverse.
A portion of the arrival surface segment.

CodeTrajectoryElementType-DEPARTURE_SURF.comment: This segment describes the elements of the overall trajectory from the departure gate up to and including the departure runway.
A portion of the departure surface segment.

CodeTrajectoryElementType-TAXI_PATH.comment: Part of the agreed 4D trajectory for both Departure and Arrival surface segments.

CodeTrajectoryElementType-TAXI_PATH_ELEM.comment: A portion of the taxi path.

CodeTrajectoryPointAcceptanceStatusType-.comment: The trajectory point has been accepted by the FDMP for the computation of the planned trajectory.
The expanded route point has been rejected by the FDMP for the computation of the planned trajectory.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-ADEP.comment: An estimated trajectory point belonging to the adep.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-ADES.comment: An estimated trajectory point belonging to the ades.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-BEACON.comment: A trajectory point corresponding to a beacon overfly.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-BEGIN_STAY_POINT.comment: The point at which the flight is expected to begin an operation at which the flight will remain for some time.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-BOTTOM_OF_CLIMB.comment: A trajectory point marking the transition from a cruise phase to a climb phase.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-BOTTOM_OF_DESCEN.comment: A trajectory point marking the transition from a descent phase to a cruise phase.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-BOUNDARY_POINT.comment: A trajectory point at which the 4D Trajectory intersects the boundary of an airspace.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-CONSTRAINT_POINT.comment: The point of application of a constraint.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-CROSSING_INTO_CO.comment: The point at which the trajectory is projected to cross into a constrained airspace.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-CROSSOVER_ALTITU.comment: The point in climb or descent where the aircraft will transition between Mach and IAS control.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-END_OF_LANDING_R.comment: The point at which the aircraft is predicted to come to a full stop on the arrival runway.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-END_OF_TURN.comment: A trajectory point corresponding to the end of a turn.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-END_PREDICTION_P.comment: The final point at which a prediction was made.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-END_STAY_POINT.comment: The point at which the flight is expected to terminate an operation at which it remained for some time.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-EXIT_FROM_CONSTR.comment: The point at which the trajectory is projected to exit from designated constrained airspace.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-FIR_BOUNDARY_CRO.comment: The point at which the trajectory crosses from one FIR into another.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-FROM_GAT_TO_OAT_.comment: A trajectory point at which the flight passes from GAT to OAT rules, indicating the start of a military portion of the route.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-FROM_IFR_TO_VFR_.comment: A trajectory point at which the flight passes from IFR to VFR rules, indicating the start of a VFR portion of the route.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-FROM_OAT_TO_GAT_.comment: A trajectory point at which the flight passes from OAT to GAT rules, indicating the end of a military portion of the route.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-FROM_VFR_TO_IFR_.comment: A trajectory point at which the flight passes from VFR to IFR rules, indicating the end of VFR portion of the route.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-HOLD_ENTRY_POINT.comment: The point at which the flight is expected to enter into planned holding.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-HOLD_EXIT_POINT.comment: The point at which the flight is expected to exit from planned holding.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-INITIAL_PREDICTI.comment: The initial point at which a prediction was made.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-INTERMEDIATE_POI.comment: A specific kind of point of the trajectory that represents no significant point, only a point that will be overflown.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-MIDDLE_OF_TURN.comment: A trajectory point corresponding to a middle of a turn.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-START_OF_TAKEOFF.comment: The trajectory point at the start of take-off roll.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-START_OF_TURN.comment: A trajectory point corresponding to a start of a turn.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-STAR_ENTRY.comment: The trajectory point corresponding to either the STAR entry point or the last point of the route (if no STAR is used).

CodeTrajectoryPointType-TOP_OF_CLIMB.comment: The trajectory point at which the trajectory arrives at the cruise flight level. There will be one top-of-climb for each cruise flight level (step climbs).

CodeTrajectoryPointType-TOP_OF_DESCENT.comment: The trajectory point at which the trajectory begins a descent from the cruise flight level.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-TRAJECTORY_CHANG.comment: A trajectory point at which an altitude level-off will be initiated or terminated, at which the speed target (Indicated or Mach) will change to a new target, or at which the course is expected to change.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-TRANSITION_ALTIT.comment: The point at which the trajectory reaches the transition altitude (in climb) or level (in descent).

CodeTrajectoryPointType-UNPUBLISHED_ROUT.comment: A trajectory point in the route that represents an unpublished point.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-WHEELS_OFF_POINT.comment: The point at which the aircraft is predicted to be wheels off the runway on departure.

CodeTrajectoryPointType-WHEELS_ON_POINT.comment: The point at which the aircraft is predicted to be wheels on the runway for arrival.

CodeTrajectorySegmentType-DIRECT_FLIGHT_.comment: A direct flight (DCT) between two specified significant points.

CodeTrajectoryType-AIRCRAFT_INTENT.comment: Information on planned future aircraft behaviour, which can be obtained from the aircraft systems (avionics). It is associated with the commanded trajectory and will enhance airborne functions. The aircraft intent data correspond either to aircraft trajectory data that directly relate to the future aircraft trajectory as programmed inside the avionics, or the aircraft control parameters as managed by the automatic flight control system. These aircraft control parameters could either be entered by the flight crew or automatically derived by the flight management system.

CodeTrajectoryType-DESIRED_4D_TRAJECTORY.comment: The current 4D trajectory that is requested and generated by the airspace user with knowledge of the ATM System's operational constraints and resource contention.

CodeTrajectoryType-EXECUTED_4D_TRAJECTOR.comment: The actual 4D trajectory of the aircraft from the start-up to the present position.

CodeTrajectoryType-EXPANDED_ROUTE.comment: The expansion of the Flight Planned Route into a set of route points.

CodeTrajectoryType-FLIGHT_PLANNED_ROUTE.comment: The description of the trajectory of a flight as filed in a flight plan.

CodeTrajectoryType-NOMINAL_PREFERRED_ROU.comment: Preferred user route in nominal conditions (e.g. meteorological).

CodeTrajectoryType-USER_PREFERRED_TRAJEC.comment: A trajectory initially provided by the Airspace User which may be amended during planning phase to integrate ATM constraints from DCB and during execution phase to integrate new ATM constraints from dynamic DCB. Alternate user preferred trajectory may be associated to the RBT/RMT to face pre-defined scenarios.

CodeTransponderType-MODE_1.comment: Mode 1 provides 2-digit 5-bit mission code. (military only - cockpit selectable)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_2.comment: Mode 2 provides 4-digit octal unit code. (military only - set on ground for fighters, can be changed in flight by transport aircraft)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_3A.comment: Mode 3/A provides a 4-digit octal identification code for the aircraft, assigned by the air traffic controller. (military and civilian)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_4.comment: Mode 4 provides a 3-pulse reply to crypto coded challenge. (military only)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_5.comment: Mode 5 provides a cryptographically secured version of Mode S and ADS-B GPS position. (military only)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_C.comment: Mode C provides 4-digit octal code for aircraft's pressure altitude. (military and civilian)

CodeTransponderType-MODE_S.comment: Mode S provides multiple information formats to a selective interrogation. Each aircraft is assigned a fixed 24-bit address. (military and civilian) Mode S, or mode select, despite also being called a transponder radar system replacement for Air Traffic Control Radar Beacon System (ATCRBS), is actually a data packet protocol which can be used to augment ATCRBS transponder positioning equipment (radar and TCAS). Mode S is designed to fully interface with ATCRBS systems: mode S SSRs can interrogate ATCRBS transponders, and AIS-P transponders will also reply to older ATCRBS and TCAS interrogations.

CodeTurbulenceType-CLEAR_AIR_TURBULENCE.comment: Upper-atmospheric turbulence encountered by an aircraft when flying through clear air.

CodeTurbulenceType-IN_CLOUD_TURBULENCE.comment: Upper-atmospheric turbulence encountered by an aircraft when flying through a cloud.

CodeTypeOfTaxiRouteType-TAXI_IN_TO_RUNWA.comment: Taxiway Route from Stand to Runway.

CodeTypeOfTaxiRouteType-TAXI_OUT_OF_RUNW.comment: Taxiway Route from Runway to Stand.

CodeUnitDependencyType-ALTERNATE.comment: The RelatedUnit provide an alternate/replacement service to the current Unit.

CodeUnitDependencyType-OWNER.comment: The Unit is owned by (subordinated to) the RelatedUnit.

CodeUnitDependencyType-PROVIDER.comment: In the provision of its services, the Unit uses the services of the RelatedUnit.

CodeUnitType-ACC.comment: A unit established to provide air traffic control service to controlled flights in control areas under its jurisdiction.

CodeUnitType-ALPS.comment: Any facility intended to serve as an intermediary between a person reporting an emergency and a rescue coordination centre or rescue subcentre.

CodeUnitType-ATFMU.comment: A unit in charge of providing Air Traffic Flow Management.

CodeUnitType-ATSU.comment: A generic term meaning variously, air traffic control unit, flight information centre or air traffic services reporting office.

CodeUnitType-BOF.comment: Briefing office (note: Note ICAO listed by nonetheless used.)

CodeUnitType-COM.comment: An aeronautical fixed station which relays or retransmits telecommunication traffic from (or to) a number of other aeronautical fixed stations directly connected to it.

CodeUnitType-FIC.comment: A unit established to provide flight information service and alerting service.

CodeUnitType-FMP.comment: A working position established in appropriate air traffic control units to ensure the necessary interface between local ATFCM partners (i.e. ATCs, AOs and Airports) and a central management unit on matters concerning the provision of the air traffic flow and capacity management service.

CodeUnitType-MET.comment: An office designated to provide meteorological service for international air navigation.

CodeUnitType-MILITARY.comment: Military station/unit (or military office in general).

CodeUnitType-MILOPS.comment: Planning/briefing office for military flight operations.

CodeUnitType-MWO.comment: An office designated to provide information concerning the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified en-route weather and other phenomena in the atmosphere that may affect the safety of aircraft operations within its specified area of responsibility.

CodeUnitType-NOF.comment: An office designated by a State for the exchange of NOTAM internationally.

CodeUnitType-RCC.comment: A unit responsible for promoting efficient organization of search and rescue services and for coordinating the conduct of search and rescue operations within a search and rescue region.

CodeUnitType-TWR.comment: A unit established to provide air traffic control service to aerodrome traffic.

CodeUnitType-VAAC.comment: A meteorological centre designated by regional air navigation agreement to provide advisory information to meteorological watch offices, area control centres, flight information centres, world area forecast centres and international OPMET databanks regarding the lateral and vertical extent and forecast movement of volcanic ash in the atmosphere following volcanic eruptions.

CodeUnitType-WAFC.comment: A meteorological centre designated to prepare and issue significant weather forecasts and upper-air forecasts in digital form on a global basis direct to States by appropriate means as part of the aeronautical fixed service.

CodeUsageLimitationType-CONDITIONAL.comment: Permission but with additional instructions. Failure to comply with the additional instructions invalidates the permission.

CodeVASISType-AVASIS.comment: Abbreviated visual approach slow indicator system.

CodeVASISType-ILU.comment: A number of identical light units.

CodeVASISType-LCVASI.comment: Low cost visual approach slope indicator: 3 sets of 4 white lights on 3 mounts usually on only one side of the runway.

CodeVASISType-OLS.comment: Optical landing system for strip decks and aircraft carriers (sometimes available on ground air bases for training purposes).

CodeVASISType-PVASI.comment: Pulsating/steady burning visual approach slope indicator, normally a single light unit projecting two colours.

CodeVASISType-TRCV.comment: Tri-colour visual approach slope indicator, normally a single light unit projecting three colours.

CodeValidityPeriodInterpretationType-BAS.comment: The baseline contains the state of an entity during a time period or a time instant, merging any permanent changes.

CodeValidityPeriodInterpretationType-PER.comment: The data describes the permanent change of an entity.

CodeValidityPeriodInterpretationType-SNA.comment: The snapshot contains the state of an entity at a time instant, merging any permanent changes and temporary changes.

CodeValidityPeriodInterpretationType-STR.comment: The stream contains the state of an entity during a time period, merging any permanent changes and temporary changes.

CodeValidityPeriodInterpretationType-TEM.comment: The data describes the temporary change of an entity.

CodeValueInterpretationType-AT_OR_ABOVE.comment: Equal to or higher than the value.

CodeValueInterpretationType-AT_OR_BELOW.comment: Equal to or lower than the value.

CodeVerticalDatumType-EGM_96.comment: Earth gravitational model 1996. ICAO recommended vertical datum.

CodeVerticalReferenceType-MSL.comment: The average location of the interface between the ocean and the atmosphere, over a period of time sufficiently long so that all random and periodic variations of short duration average to zero.

CodeVerticalReferenceType-SFC.comment: The distance measured from the surface of the Earth (equivalent to AGL - Above Ground Level).

CodeVerticalReferenceType-STD.comment: The vertical distance is measured with an altimeter set to the standard atmosphere.

CodeVerticalReferenceType-WGS84.comment: WGS84 is an Earth-centered, Earth-fixed terrestrial reference system and geodetic datum adopted as the common geodetic reference frame for civil aviation.

CodeVerticalStructureMarkingType-CHEQUER.comment: Markings painted in a chequered pattern.

CodeVerticalStructureMarkingType-MARKERS.comment: Marks attached to cables or wires.

CodeVerticalStructureMarkingType-MONOCOL.comment: Markings painted as a single colour.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-ADOBE_.comment: Brick made of adobe clay and straw, dried in the sun rather than by oven firing (as are standard bricks). Larger than standard bricks, adobe bricks require a type of clay that contains between 25 and 45 percent aluminium salts.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-ALUMIN.comment: A light silvery ductile and malleable metal, not readily tarnished by air, which is a chemical element, atomic number 13. (Symbol Al)

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-BRICK.comment: Clay kneaded, moulded, and baked or sun-dried, used as a building material.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-CONCRE.comment: A heavy-duty building material made from a mixture of broken stone or gravel, sand, cement and water, that forms a stone like mass on hardening.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-FIBREG.comment: Any material consisting of glass filaments woven into a textile or paper, or embedded in plastic, for use as a construction or insulation material.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-GLASS.comment: A substance made by fusing soda and/or potash with other ingredients. Usually transparent, lustrous, hard, and brittle.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-IRON.comment: A malleable, magnetic, readily oxidizable metal which is a chemical element of the transition series, atomic number 26. (Symbol Fe) Occurs abundantly in certain ores and in meteorites, and is widely used, chiefly in alloys such as steel.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-MASONR.comment: Building materials (for example: stone, brick, concrete, hollow-tile, concrete block, gypsum block, or other similar building units or materials and/or combination of the same) bonded together with mortar to form a structure (for example: a wall, a pier).

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-METAL.comment: Any of the class of substances that are characteristically lustrous, ductile, fusible, malleable solids and are good conductors of heat and electricity. For example, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin, and certain alloys (as brass and bronze).

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-MUD.comment: Constructed principally from mud applied to a structural scaffold of plant material (for example: wooden posts). Effective only in extremely dry climates and usually must be resurfaced on a regular basis (for example: yearly) otherwise the structure steadily disintegrates under the effect of weather.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-PLANT.comment: Plant material (for example: straw and/or tall coarse grass), possibly also containing the slices of soil to which the plant material is attached. For example, used in thatching or sodding a roof.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-PRESTR.comment: Reinforced concrete in which internal stresses have been introduced to reduce potential tensile stress in the concrete resulting from loads.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-REINFO.comment: Poured concrete containing steel bars or metal netting to increase its tensile strength.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-SOD.comment: A usually square or oblong piece or slice of earth together with the grass growing on it.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-STEEL.comment: Any of numerous artificially produced alloys of iron containing up to 3 per cent of other elements (including less than about 2.2 per cent carbon) and having great strength and malleability. Able to be tempered to many different degrees of hardness. Used for making tools, weapons, and/or machinery.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-STONE.comment: Pieces of rock or mineral substance (other than metal) of definite form and size, usually artificially shaped, and used for some special purpose. Used, for example, for building, for paving, or in the form of a block, slab, or pillar set up as a memorial and/or a boundary-mark.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-TREATE.comment: A timber that has been impregnated with chemicals (for example: creosote oil) to reduce damage from wood rot and/or insects. Often used for the portions of a structure that are likely to be in ongoing contact with soil and/or water.

CodeVerticalStructureMaterialType-WOOD.comment: The hard, compact, fibrous substance of which the roots, trunks, and branches of trees and shrubs consist. Consists largely of secondary xylem, which forms the strengthening and water-transporting tissue of the plant.

CodeVerticalStructureType-COMPRESSED_AIR.comment: AirMAT: The components of a compressed air system.

CodeVerticalStructureType-CONTROL_MONITO.comment: AirMAT: The components of an electronic monitoring and control system (EMCS) including cables, devices, and so on.

CodeVerticalStructureType-ELECTRICAL_EXI.comment: AirMAT: The components of an electrical exterior lighting system including cables, switches, devices, transformers, and so on. Does not include field, navaid, or approach lighting

CodeVerticalStructureType-ELECTRICAL_SYS.comment: AirMAT: The components of an electrical distribution system including cables, switches, devices, motors, transformers, and so on.

CodeVerticalStructureType-FIXED_BASE_OPE.comment: FBOs support GA and business aviation operations by providing maintenance, fueling, flight planning, and local ground transportation services. FBOs are typically located away from the commercial concourse/stand areas while still having access to active taxiways and runways.

CodeVerticalStructureType-FUEL_SYSTEM.comment: AirMAT: The components of a fuel distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, pumps, tanks, and so on

CodeVerticalStructureType-GATE.comment: Area of a fence which may be opened for passage through the fence or closed to prevent passage through the fence.

CodeVerticalStructureType-GENERAL_UTILIT.comment: AirMAT: The components of utility system which are universal in use and purpose and do not belong to a specific utility

CodeVerticalStructureType-HEAT_COOL_SYST.comment: AirMAT: The components of a heating and cooling distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on.

CodeVerticalStructureType-INDUSTRIAL_SYS.comment: AirMAT: The components of an industrial waste collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, tanks, lagoons, and so on.

CodeVerticalStructureType-NATURAL_GAS_SY.comment: AirMAT: The components of a natural gas distribution system consisting of pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on.

CodeVerticalStructureType-SALTWATER_SYST.comment: AirMAT: The components of a salt water collection system.

CodeVerticalStructureType-STORM_SYSTEM.comment: AirMAT: The components of a storm drainage collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, and so on).

CodeVerticalStructureType-TERMINAL.comment: Aerodrome terminal. A terminal is a facility to handle arriving, transit, or departing passengers. As such, multiple terminals may share a single physical building, but are separate if passengers are not allowed to move freely between them. There is implicitly always at least one terminal in an aerodrome.

CodeVerticalStructureType-WASTEWATER_SYS.comment: AirMAT: The components of a wastewater collection system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, treatment plants, collection locations, and so forth.

CodeVerticalStructureType-WATER_SYSTEM.comment: AirMAT: The components of a water system including pipes, fittings, fixtures, treatment plants, and so on.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-AGNIS.comment: Azimuth Guidance for Nose-In Stand, providing centreline guidance only by using two coloured lights mounted side by side.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-AGNIS_STOP.comment: AGNIS system complemented with a simple stop light, on the side of the AGNIS display.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-APIS.comment: Aircraft Positioning and Information System that shows azimuth information using a series of parallel and black bars which kink at their midpoint.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-A_VDGS.comment: Advanced Visual Docking Guidance System that features electronic displays which perform the functions of an AGNIS/PAPA installation, although with much greater accuracy. They may also provide collision avoidance from static objects.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-PAPA.comment: Parallax Aircraft Parking Aid consisting of a large grey/black box that uses the effect of perspective in order to indicate the relative position of the aircraft along the centreline.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-SAFE_DOC.comment: Safe dock allows aircraft to park up to an accuracy of 10 cm using lasers to attain the aircraft's position.

CodeVisualDockingGuidanceType-SAFE_GATE.comment: A type of A-VDGS that uses an aircraft symbol on a display indicating the relative position along the centreline.

CodeWakeTurbulenceCategoryType-HEAVY.comment: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 136000 kg or more.

CodeWakeTurbulenceCategoryType-LIGHT.comment: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of 7000 kg or less.

CodeWakeTurbulenceCategoryType-MEDIUM.comment: An aircraft type with a maximum certified take-off mass of less than 136000 kg. but more than 7000 kg.

CodeWakeTurbulenceCategoryType-SUPER.comment: A SUPER HEAVY aircraft type e.g. the Airbus A380-800. (In the order of 560,000kg).

CodeWakeTurbulenceCategoryType-UNDEFINED.comment: Not defined, none of the other values is applicable: applicable for AircraftTypes for which it is not clear whether the WTC is light, medium or heavy (e.g. helicopters). There is no relationship with the maximum certified take-off mass.

CodeWakeVortexClassificationType-MH.comment: Medium when Trailing; Heavy when Leading.

CodeWeatherIntensityType-NONE.comment: A report of no intensity (no icing present, for example) for a condition. This is different from missing information.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-DUST_STORM.comment: An ensemble of particles of dust energetically lifted to great heights by a strong and turbulent wind.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-DUST_WHIRL.comment: An ensemble of particles of dust or sand, sometimes accompanied by small litter, raised from the ground in the form of a whirling column of varying height with a small diameter and an approximately vertical axis.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-FUNNEL_CLOUD.comment: Cloud formed at the core of a waterspout or tornado vortex, sometimes extending right down to the ground, caused by the reduction of pressure at the centre of the vortex.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-LIGHTNING.comment: Luminous manifestation accompanying a sudden electrical discharge which takes place from or inside a cloud or, less often, from high structures on the ground or from mountains.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-MOUNTAIN_OBSCU.comment: Description of a visibility condition that is distinguished from IFR because ceilings, by definition, are described as "above ground level" (AGL). In mountainous terrain clouds can form at altitudes significantly higher than the weather reporting station and at the same time nearby mountain tops may be obscured by low visibility. In these areas the ground level can also vary greatly over a small area.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-MOUNTAIN_WAVE.comment: Atmospheric internal gravity waves, which are periodic changes of atmospheric pressure, temperature and orthometric height in a current of air.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-RADIOACTIVE_CL.comment: A radioactive particulate contaminated atmospheric area.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-SANDSTORM.comment: An ensemble of particles of sand energetically lifted to great heights by a strong and turbulent wind.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-SQUALL.comment: Atmospheric phenomenon characterized by an abrupt and large increase of wind speed with a duration of the order of minutes which diminishes rather suddenly. It is often accompanied by showers or thunderstorms.

CodeWeatherPhenomenonType-TEMPERATURE_IN.comment: Vertical temperature distribution such that temperature increases with height.

CodeWindCharacteristicType-100_KNOTS.comment: Forecasted wind on airport surface is more than 100kt (200 Km/h)

CodeWindCharacteristicType-CALM.comment: Wind direction on airport surface is irrelevant, wind is less than 1kt

CodeWindCharacteristicType-NORMAL.comment: Wind on airport surface is normally described through the direction attribute

CodeWindCharacteristicType-VRB.comment: Wind direction on airport surface is variable

CodeWorkAreaType-CONSTRUCTION.comment: The work area is used for construction.

CodeWorkAreaType-PARKED_AIRCRAFT.comment: Parked or disabled aircraft or machinery.

CodeWorkAreaType-SURFACE_WORK.comment: The work area is used for surface improvements.

known_limitations: AIRM-O is an external EUROCONTROL/AIRM-derived ontology, not a NASA/FAA data source.
Alignment cells are schema-level references and require review before runtime validation use.
